papers.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models

summary.tldr: FRED improves World Action Models by self-distilling future video representations from noise in a single denoising step using ground-truth targets and historical context.
key_points: FRED conditions video diffusion models on historical observations to supply temporal context for predicting future representations.
Uses a self-distillation objective where representations extracted from ground-truth future observations act as targets for single-step noise predictions.
Eliminates the need for iterative video denoising during action prediction by training the action decoder on single-step future representations.
Achieved 50.0% task success on zero-shot human-to-robot skill transfer tasks lacking robot training data, compared to 19.4% for the top competing baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables fast, real-time robot policy inference while significantly improving zero-shot generalization and human-to-robot skill transfer.

papers.title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography

summary.tldr: FilmFlow is an agentic framework that converts natural-language instructions or reference videos into executable 3D camera trajectories by orchestrating multi-agent planning and feedback loop refinement.
key_points: A Director agent constructs executable camera plans by composing concurrent atomic operations for translation, rotation, and framing.
The framework incorporates three supporting specialized agents: an Interpreter (intent extraction), a Scout (initial viewpoint selection), and a Critic (evaluates renders for iterative refinement).
Introduces CinemaBench, featuring 150 Blender scenes with 750 text-directed tasks and 60 reference videos to evaluate text- and video-directed camera trajectory generation.
Outperformed evaluated baselines on CinemaBench in spatial reasoning, temporal coordination, visual composition, and human user preference.
summary.why_it_matters: FilmFlow bridges the gap between high-level cinematographic intent and executable 3D camera trajectories, enabling automated, controllable virtual film production.

papers.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems

summary.tldr: A study quantifies 'mosaic effect' confidentiality leaks in LLM agents, where models infer and disclose forbidden composite conclusions from accessible documents even under benign queries and explicit aggregation safeguards.
key_points: Evaluated 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military scenarios generating 10,800 simulated answers across three LLM agents and 1,440 answers across two live open-source harnesses.
The top model, GPT-5.6-Sol, disclosed forbidden composite information in 7.08% of benign query answers during controlled simulations, with higher disclosure rates in live environments.
Applying classification headers and explicit aggregation rules reduced pooled disclosures, but unsafe disclosures still persisted in 32.37% of simulated answers across all intents.
Increased model refusals failed to protect confidentiality, as significant refusals often revealed the prohibited conclusions directly.
summary.why_it_matters: LLM agents operating in mixed-clearance environments present a structural data leak risk by inferring sensitive conclusions from unclassified documents, which standard classification headers and refusals fail to fully mitigate.

papers.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought

summary.tldr: Raw-RAG outperforms complex agentic memory systems across multiple long-term conversation benchmarks by leveraging dense retrieval and reranking directly over raw, unmutated conversation histories.
key_points: Raw-RAG uses dense retrieval and reranking over raw history without relying on memory mutation, structural organization, or learned retrieval strategies.
Raw-RAG ranked first in six out of seven benchmark-model settings across LoCoMo, LongMemEval, MEME, and MemoryAgentBench.
Raw-RAG outperformed the strongest agentic memory baseline by 0.13 to 5.53 points.
Higher evidence coverage in raw history offsets lower evidence utilization, as transformed memory stores lose vital answer values, relations, and dependency paths.
summary.why_it_matters: This demonstrates that complex, resource-intensive agentic memory operations are often unnecessary, making naive RAG a crucial baseline for long-term LLM conversation tasks.

papers.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

summary.tldr: RLSplat is a resource-linear feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that reduces inference latency, peak memory, and output size proportionally with lower target Gaussian budgets.
key_points: Replaces conventional dense-prediction and post-pruning approaches with a dynamic Gaussian allocation policy that predicts only the exact target count of Gaussians.
Utilizes a resource-linear Gaussian decoding process where each primitive attends exclusively to nearby Gaussians identified via a hierarchical neighbor search.
Outperforms existing budget-controllable methods in zero-shot evaluations across all Gaussian budgets, exceeding the top baseline's performance while using 4x fewer Gaussians.
Achieves up to a 4.1x reduction in inference latency and a 9.6x reduction in peak memory consumption at lower budget thresholds.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deployable feed-forward 3D reconstruction on memory-constrained edge devices by scaling inference computation and memory directly with the allocated Gaussian budget.

papers.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression

summary.tldr: TTR-Compressor introduces sequence compression via end-to-end learned test-time regression, computing compressed token coefficients in closed form during the forward pass.
key_points: Replaces standard pooling and MLP projections by framing input tokens as a regression problem solved in closed form during inference.
Learns the regression problem formulation end-to-end via standard backpropagation.
Outperforms attention-based compressors on the RULER benchmark when used for block-wise sparse attention.
Matches standard MLP visual token merger performance in multimodal LLMs while using 55.6% fewer visual tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a more parameter-efficient compression primitive that significantly reduces token counts in multimodal LLMs and sparse attention without sacrificing performance.

papers.title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos

summary.tldr: Verus-Insight improves AI-generated video detection by decomposing artifact analysis into Inspection Planning, Evidence Verification, and Evidence Aggregation using progressive capability training.
key_points: Formulates artifact detection into three structured stages: Inspection Planning (determining targets), Evidence Verification (checking for actual artifacts), and Evidence Aggregation (making the final video-level decision).
Trains the Verus-Insight model using human-anchored full-process supervision combined with progressive capability training.
Introduces Verus-Bench, a dedicated benchmark containing fine-grained human annotations of perceptible visual artifacts.
Converts inspection targets into verified evidence more reliably while mitigating spurious artifact claims compared to existing detectors.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a structured, explainable framework for deepfake and synthetic video detection that grounds final classification decisions in verified visual evidence rather than opaque heuristics.

papers.title: AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark

summary.tldr: AnyGameRenderer is a video-to-video generative rendering model that turns low-fidelity game blockouts into high-quality video while maintaining strict entity-level correspondence and layout timing.
key_points: Fine-tunes the 33B MiniMax-H3 ref2va reference-video-conditioned model using LoRA.
Trained on 10k paired clips sourced from GEAR agent-made games, controlled Unreal Engine crowd streams, and real gameplay paired via 3D-box detection.
Accepts raw video inputs like gray blockouts, semantic maps, and wireframes without requiring engine G-buffers, class labels, or low-poly proxies.
Evaluated on a 59-case, 753-entity benchmark, improving temporal match rate from 50.9% to 62.9% and reducing missed count changes from 34.7% to 21.3% over the base model.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables AI agents to generate visual assets for diverse game genres without losing precise control over spatial layout, entity counts, or object timing.

papers.title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding

summary.tldr: AgentVQA is a unified offline benchmark containing 1,000 real-world examples across five agent domains, designed to evaluate vision-language models on complex agentic visual understanding.
key_points: Consolidates 1,000 manually selected, challenging agent examples adapted from 23 source datasets across five domains: Web Agents, Robotics, Egocentric Videos, Games, and Spatial Planning.
Provides offline evaluation model rankings that reliably correlate with performance in corresponding online environments.
Evaluated 22 models, with the top-performing model reaching only 58.5% accuracy.

Identifies visual state grounding as the main bottleneck, with failures occurring in UI localization, motion interpretation, temporal state tracking, and 3D spatial inference, rather than reasoning errors.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a scalable, low-cost offline benchmark that accurately mirrors online agent performance while pinpointing visual state representation as the primary failure mode in current vision-language models.

papers.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: T2Quant is a novel framework for Diffusion Language Models that optimizes mixed-precision activation quantization by dynamically allocating bit-widths based on label-free task and timestep sensitivity signals.
key_points: Diffusion Language Model (DLM) quantization sensitivity varies across downstream tasks and temporal denoising steps.
Quantization sensitivity patterns across time and tasks can be predicted without relying on ground-truth labels or task-specific metrics.
T2Quant allocates activation precision under a fixed bit-width budget using this label-free sensitivity signal.
Evaluations across three DLMs and six benchmarks show accuracy improvements up to 6.7 percentage points over existing methods under identical bit-width budgets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables higher accuracy and efficiency in DLM inference by dynamically targeting precision where and when it is most needed without requiring labeled evaluation data.

papers.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models

summary.tldr: A study reveals that reasoning models inherit the "{wait}" pause marker from training data rather than inventing it via reinforcement learning, showing large RL accuracy gains can occur entirely without the word.
key_points: RL raises MATH-500 accuracy without coining the "{wait}" marker on base models that lack it.
The marker enters models through mid-training data (e.g., OLMo-3) or supervised fine-tuning on reasoning traces.
Released RL-Zero recipes (OLMo-3, MiMo) multiply the marker's presence, whereas KL-free GRPO does not.
GRPO applied after supervised fine-tuning can erase the marker entirely, and RL-Zero recipes can degrade its structural form.
Automated LLM-as-a-judge revision metrics can reverse human-labeled trends when assessing reasoning markers.
summary.why_it_matters: Marker frequency is an unreliable indicator of RL-driven reasoning, highlighting that model behaviors attributed to RL discovery may simply be artifacts inherited from supervised pre-training or fine-tuning datasets.

papers.title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention

summary.tldr: RIDAR is a new framework that uses the 14-type RIVT taxonomy to detect research integrity violations in autonomous agents post-hoc and dynamically correct them during runtime.
key_points: RIVT provides a taxonomy of 14 research integrity violation (RIV) types spanning the complete research lifecycle.

RIDAR-post-hoc achieves an 85.2% F1 score on the expert-annotated RIV-Gold benchmark (60 trajectories) and detected 3,964 RIV instances across 99.7% of trajectories in the RIV-Wild dataset (300 trajectories, 50 tasks).
RIDAR-runtime dynamically detects and fixes RIVs during agent execution, reducing remaining RIVs at task completion by 36.8%.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables automated safeguards to prevent autonomous AI research agents from producing unfaithful, unreproducible, or invalid scientific outputs.

papers.title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: A controlled study on diffusion language models reveals optimal unmasking policy design choices, resulting in an 856K-parameter policy that achieves superior speed-accuracy trade-offs across multiple benchmarks.
key_points: Labeling predictions that match the final output is overly permissive at low number of function evaluations (NFE), whereas trajectory-contraction targets maintain reference trajectory quality.
Policy inputs using hidden states alone are weak, but combining hidden states with confidence metrics provides superior unmasking performance.
A 10% reduction in NFE is sufficient to offset the computational overhead for unmasking policies with up to 7.5 million parameters.
An 856K-parameter policy trained on LLaDA-8B-Instruct achieves the best accuracy-NFE frontier on GSM8K and transfers effectively to Dream-7B-Instruct.
summary.why_it_matters: Using lightweight learned unmasking policies with the right supervision targets and input features accelerates diffusion language model inference while maintaining output quality.

papers.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation

summary.tldr: F2G-Pose is a real-time, single-pass RGB-D framework that directly predicts category-level 3D pose, metric size, and shape completion at 28 FPS.
key_points: Lifts dense features from a frozen RADIO backbone to partial point clouds and processes them with DGCNN tokenization.
Integrates object-level global structure using a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Transformer.
Enforces metric consistency using joint size prediction and camera-frame shape completion supervised by dense geometry.
Trained exclusively on synthetic SOPE pose-annotated data, setting state-of-the-art results on SOPE and ROPE while transferring to HANDAL and HouseCat6D.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates high-latency diffusion sampling and multi-stage error propagation, enabling fast and accurate category-level 3D pose estimation for real-time robotic manipulation.

papers.title: Who Takes the Lead? Model Ability and Task-Conditioned Collaboration with Humans

summary.tldr: A study using a shared-control maze reveals that stronger language-model agents dynamically condition human involvement on route advantage, while weaker models lack this selective task allocation.
key_points: Evaluated GPT 5.6 Sol, Command A+, Qwen 3.8 27B, and Command R on a shared-control maze task with varying human shortest-path advantages.
The agent allocates each team turn by deciding whether to act itself or delegate the move to the human participant.

Top-performing solo models (GPT 5.6 Sol, Command A+, Qwen 3.8 27B) selectively involved humans in ~80% of initial decisions when the human had a shorter route, but acted independently when the human had no advantage.
Command R, which demonstrated substantially weaker solo performance, failed to exhibit task-conditioned selectivity during co-play.
summary.why_it_matters: A drop in human interaction by AI agents indicates an optimal division of labor based on relative capability rather than a breakdown in collaboration.

papers.title: Multi-Token Prediction and Alternative Tokenization Improve Learning Latent Multi-Hop Graph Search at Scale

summary.tldr: Researchers overcome graph pathfinding failure modes in language models by identifying supervision signal and tokenization as orthogonal bottlenecks and solving them via multi-token prediction and alternative tokenization methods.
key_points: Identifies two distinct, orthogonal causes for language model failure on shortest-path multi-hop graph search at scale: tokenization and supervision signal quality.
Establishes theoretically and demonstrates empirically that multi-token prediction (MTP) improves learning of shortest paths.
Proves that the performance benefits derived from multi-token prediction are topologically agnostic.
Introduces alternative graph tokenizations to enable stable, consistent learning of shortest paths on unseen graphs beyond previous scale limits.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining multi-token prediction with optimized tokenizations enables language models to reliably perform complex multi-hop algorithmic reasoning over large unseen graph structures.

papers.title: SQuAT: Spherical Lattice Vector Quantization-Aware Training

summary.tldr: SQuAT scales lattice VQ-QAT to multi-billion-parameter LLMs by using separate straight-through estimators for decomposed weight directions and magnitudes alongside a distributed exact nearest-neighbor assignment scheme.
key_points: Weight vectors are decomposed into gains (quantized via low-bit scalar quantizers) and normalized directions (quantized via an E_8-derived spherical codebook).
Applying separate STEs to shape and gain induces tangent-space updates for directions, acting as an implicit form of spherical (Riemannian) optimization.
A distributed exact nearest-neighbor assignment scheme communicates only discrete indices across workers, reducing VQ-QAT training time by 12.8x and scaling to 10B tokens.
Evaluated on LLaMA-3.2-1B/3B, Qwen3-4B, and base Qwen3-1.7B, SQuAT achieved state-of-the-art VQ-QAT accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that lattice-based vector quantization can be efficiently trained at scale via quantization-aware training, enabling state-of-the-art accuracy for highly compressed low-bit LLMs.

authors: Tycho F. A. van der Ouderaa

papers.title: Harmful Responses Are Jailbreak Templates: Transferring Autoregressive Jailbreaks to Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced RMT-Jailbreak, a framework that transfers autoregressive jailbreak attacks to diffusion language models by turning harmful responses into masked templates for bidirectional reconstruction.
key_points: Identifies that masking a subset of tokens in a harmful query response creates a template that induces diffusion LLMs (dLLMs) to reconstruct harmful content.
RMT-Jailbreak converts autoregressive-generated harmful responses into high-mask-ratio templates via uniform token retention.
Applies prompt-based safety filtering to mask any remaining visible harmful content before submitting the template to the target dLLM.
Demonstrates cross-paradigm transferability of existing autoregressive jailbreak methods to dLLMs using bidirectional context modeling.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that safety alignments in diffusion LLMs can be bypassed by repurposing output templates from autoregressive LLMs, exposing a critical cross-architecture vulnerability.

papers.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization

summary.tldr: OPTIC compresses Per-Layer Embeddings up to 1,002x by storing one quantized code tuple per token and using layer-specific affine decoders fitted to the output path.
key_points: Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE) represent 35.2% of total parameters in Gemma 4 E4B.
OPTIC decodes a single token-shared code tuple at every layer using layer-specific affine decoders fitted directly to the PLE output path.
At ~100x compression on BF16 E4B, OPTIC retains 97.8% of performance across seven benchmarks versus 66.3% for product quantization.
At 594x and 1,002x compression, OPTIC maintains 90.5% and 84.1% performance retention respectively, and 96.9% retention on W4A16 E4B at ~100x.
During inference at ~100x compression, OPTIC reduces BF16 E4B GPU memory usage by 29.7% with a maximum latency overhead of 0.40%.
summary.why_it_matters: OPTIC enables massive reductions in GPU memory overhead for per-layer embedding architectures with negligible throughput loss and high performance retention.

papers.title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation

summary.tldr: Cola2 introduces a hierarchical language modeling framework using dynamic continuous semantic compression and a block-causal masked diffusion decoder, demonstrating strong performance and unsaturated scaling compared to standard autoregressive models.
key_points: Text is dynamically segmented into semantic spans with compression rates managed via auxiliary-loss-free negative feedback.

The decoder uses a block-causal masked diffusion architecture trained with clean, noisy, and dropped latent conditions, employing classifier-free guidance to balance reconstruction and autonomous generation.
Token-prediction gradients update the encoder through latents, while Flow Matching prior learning is decoupled from representation learning via a stop-gradient.
Inference re-encodes generated text under a fixed span layout to maintain continuous latent history consistency with actual text context.
An unconverged checkpoint trained on 346.03 billion tokens achieved a 60.10 average across eight tasks, outperforming Llama-3-8B on HellaSwag and StoryCloze.
summary.why_it_matters: Cola2 proves that continuous-latent hierarchical generation can match or exceed massive autoregressive baselines like Llama-3-8B while utilizing a fraction of the pretraining compute budget.

papers.title: Mixing Matters: Evidence Position Bias Across Sequence Mixers in Long-Context Question Answering

summary.tldr: A comparative study reveals Transformers exhibit a context-beginning position bias absent in pure state-space models, though both families maintain a context-ending bias in long-context question answering.
key_points: Evaluated Transformers show both beginning and end-of-context accuracy advantages, whereas evaluated state-space models (Mamba) lack the beginning advantage while maintaining the end advantage.
Prompt engineering and variations can create or nearly eliminate the beginning position bias in evaluated architectures.
Absolute position information remains decodable across both Transformer and state-space architectures, even when final response performance curves diverge.
Attention concentration near initial tokens correlates with context-beginning sensitivity within the tested Transformer model family.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that position bias varies by model family, prompt structure, and attention allocation helps engineers better optimize context layout and architecture choices for long-document tasks.

papers.title: Delta N-gram: Forward-Only Continual Writing into a Language Model's Native N-gram Memory

summary.tldr: Delta N-gram introduces a forward-only continual write path into a language model's frozen native hashed N-gram table using a 4.1M-parameter writer to emit gated target updates into a sparse delta patch.
key_points: The method keeps the pretrained table T^0 intact and writes updates to a sparse patch Δ via a block-averaged delta rule, allowing instant restoration of the base model by clearing Δ.
On a 0.6B prototype, Delta N-gram retains 16/16 written facts after a second write, outperforming online gradient writes which retain only 2 to 4 facts.
Evaluating a delta writer on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next over 35,000 writes yields stable execution with late-task accuracy dropping by only 0.52 percentage points compared to -7.29pp for gradient updates.
General-input drift (reaching 32.8%) is driven by format rows that expand 4 to 12 times their pretrained norm; zeroing eight key format rows eliminates over 98% of layer-2 drift on math inputs.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables rapid, stable, and reversible continual knowledge updates in language models without requiring backpropagation or catastrophic forgetting of base capabilities.

papers.title: RIFT: KV Cache Compression for Draft Models with Complementary Compressibility Training

summary.tldr: RIFT introduces adaptive KV cache refreshing and sparse-attention compressibility training to mitigate decode staleness in speculative decoding draft models.
key_points: Identifies decode staleness, where prefill-focused selection-based KV cache compression degrades draft model accuracy as output length increases.
Proposes RIFT, a selection-based KV cache compression strategy that balances prefill tokens with recently generated tokens through periodic KV cache selection refreshes.
Introduces an adaptive KV refresh mechanism to minimize score re-calculation overhead while maintaining target drafter quality.
Implements a compressibility-driven training phase using sparse attention masks to optimize the draft model for operation under constrained KV cache sizes.
Enables a Qwen3.5-4B draft model serving Qwen3.5-122B to retain over 98% of its full-cache acceptance length on 32K input/4K output sequences using an 8K KV cache budget.
summary.why_it_matters: It dramatically reduces memory consumption during long-output speculative decoding without sacrificing the acceptance rate or speedup of the draft model.

papers.title: What Pairwise Evaluation Misses: Reward Scores across Prompts

summary.tldr: A study reveals pairwise evaluation masks prompt-level reward model errors, showing models over-cluster scores by prompt (shares of 0.34 to 0.64 on HelpSteer2) compared to near-zero human rating variation.
key_points: Pairwise evaluation cancels out prompt-shared score components, leaving prompt-level variance untested.
The authors introduce a human-referenced audit comprising between-prompt variance share, sibling-rating regression, and prompt substitutions.
Evaluation of 18 released scorers shows RM scores cluster by prompt significantly more than human ratings (0.34-0.64 vs near zero on HelpSteer2).
Replacing prompts with a fixed instruction maintains score clustering but reduces alignment with human prompt-level ratings.
Subtracting prompt means degrades global response selection helpfulness, indicating part of the between-prompt variation is functional.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating reward models solely via pairwise comparisons hides prompt-level score distortions, requiring separate audits for between-prompt variation, prompt sensitivity, and global selection utility.

papers.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: METTA is a meta-reinforcement learning framework that decomposes fast adaptation into linear-complexity within-episode causal neural memory and compact cross-episode summaries for efficient long-context task inference.
key_points: Decomposes adaptation into two temporal scales: causal neural memory for fine-grained within-episode adaptation and compact episode-level summaries for cross-episode inference.
Replaces quadratic-cost transformer attention over full histories with linear-complexity sequence modeling to reduce memory and compute costs.
Achieves over 50% success rate on held-out Meta-World ML10/45 test environments with low training budget and short wall-clock time.
Outperforms transformer baselines on long-context sparse-reward PointMaze tasks by exhibiting more structured exploration.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables meta-RL agents to efficiently adapt to unseen long-context tasks without suffering from the quadratic computational and memory costs of transformer architectures.

security.title: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks

summary.tldr: A supply chain compromise of LiteLLM version 1.107.0 on PyPI used Python startup mechanisms to automatically execute credential-theft payloads whenever the Python interpreter initialized.
key_points: The upstream release workflow was redirected from BerriAI/litellm to a lookalike Berri-AI/litellm repository using stolen GitHub credentials.
The payload executed automatically upon Python startup via path extensions and site-specific configurations without requiring an explicit 'import litellm'.
The credential collector targeted AI applications, cloud infrastructure, browser data, SSH keys, developer tools, and LiteLLM proxy database records.
Running Python or pip inside a suspect environment triggers the malicious payload, complicating standard containment and inspection procedures.
summary.why_it_matters: Remediating this breach requires full credential rotation and environment replacement, as simply removing the package leaves systems compromised and executing routine Python commands can re-trigger the payload.

security.title: MIG-COW: Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Deepfake Detectors via Gradient Decomposition

summary.tldr: MIG-COW combines momentum-integrated gradients with consensus-orthogonal decomposition to create transferable adversarial attacks against deepfake detectors across heterogeneous CNN and ViT architectures.
key_points: Combines momentum-integrated gradients and consensus-orthogonal gradient decomposition to target shared and model-specific vulnerabilities.
Achieves a 99.96% white-box attack success rate (ASR) with high SSIM on AADD-2025 Challenge benchmarks.
Drops to a 7.16% ASR in official black-box evaluations, illustrating persistent transferability challenges.
Demonstrates that including low-performing, diverse models in surrogate ensembles can degrade overall attack performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals critical vulnerabilities in deepfake detection models while demonstrating that surrogate model selection and black-box transferability remain major bottlenecks for practical adversarial attacks.

security.title: Model-intrinsic, Weight-level, and Training-free Spectral Fingerprinting for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: A training-free LLM fingerprinting framework extracts weight-level spectral features from GATE projection parameters in gated FFNs to identify models without inputs, activations, or text generation.
key_points: Constructs GATE spectral scalar features directly from the singular-value distributions of GATE projection weights in gated FFNs.
Aggregates layer-wise spectral features using depth-wise segmented pooling to preserve layer-depth structure while enabling comparison across models with varying depths.
Calculates fingerprint similarity using linear centered kernel alignment (CKA).
Requires zero training, input prompts, forward-pass activations, or auxiliary verifier models.
Maintains stable similarity across post-training modifications including instruction tuning, quantization, pruning, and distillation.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables robust offline auditing and intellectual property ownership protection for open-weight LLMs without relying on brittle, generation-based behavioral queries or execution environments.

security.title: HiMark: Hierarchical and Controllable Multi-bit Watermarking for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: HiMark introduces a hierarchical and controllable multi-bit watermarking framework for LLMs that uses candidate-control mechanisms during embedding and model-agnostic evidence aggregation during detection to improve extraction accuracy.
key_points: Embedding uses a hierarchical candidate-control pipeline featuring initial candidate sampling, layer-wise tournament elimination, support-based refinement, and support-threshold filtering.
Detection uses a model-agnostic evidence aggregation mechanism that calculates multi-layer support evidence per token and accumulates votes for robust multi-bit extraction.
Achieves 90.01% watermark extraction accuracy under paraphrasing attacks when embedding 32 bits into a 300-token text.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables robust provenance tracking and accountability for LLM-generated text by allowing multi-bit metadata to survive post-processing attacks without sacrificing text quality.

security.title: Beyond End-to-End Recovery: Towards a Better Understanding of LLM Steganography via Rolewise Decomposition

summary.tldr: A rolewise decomposition framework separates encoding, decoding, and deterministic verification in LLM steganography, revealing message representations and decoder failures masked by traditional end-to-end recovery metrics.
key_points: Introduces a rolewise decomposition framework to separately evaluate how encoders represent private messages, what decoders recover, and what deterministic verification establishes.
Analysis of 7,200 encoder responses revealed 168 verifiable message encodings that decoders failed to recover.
Identified 706 responses containing private messages reconstructed via unspecified patterns, such as word-length or token-initial strategies.
Demonstrates that end-to-end recovery metrics fail to distinguish between encoding and decoding failures in LLM steganography.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating encoding and decoding separately provides a clearer understanding of covert LLM communication, which is necessary for accurately identifying and mitigating safety risks.

security.title: Not Where You Think: Protecting Location Privacy Against Reasoning-Based Geolocation

summary.tldr: Researchers developed GeoTrace, a structured reasoning attack that localizes images via visual clues, and GeoShift, a user-side defense that rewrites high-impact geographic clues to misdirect location inference.
key_points: GeoTrace performs coarse-to-fine geographic reasoning to extract visual clues from ordinary images lacking metadata or famous landmarks.
Tested on a benchmark of 525 worldwide images, GeoTrace achieved 1-km localization accuracy of 25.71% using Gemini-3-Flash and 16.95% using GPT-5-mini.
Precise localization relies disproportionately on small, editable local visual clues, while broad scene properties support coarse localization.
GeoShift breaks the clue chain by preserving stable scene properties, selecting a compatible false target, and strategically rewriting geo-revealing clues.
GeoShift reduced street-level (1 km) localization rates to 2.48% for GPT-5-mini and 3.81% for Gemini-3-Flash while preserving image quality.
summary.why_it_matters: GeoShift provides an effective, proactive user-side defense against privacy leaks caused by advanced multimodal models inferring precise real-world locations from ordinary photos.

security.title: The Psychology of an AI Hacker

summary.tldr: Researchers extracted 171 emotion directions from a 4B-parameter cybersecurity transformer (CT0/alias3-micro), finding that dynamically routing emotion steering interventions improves cybersecurity task performance on cybench-subtask by 4.2 percentage points.
key_points: Extracted 171 emotion directions from the CT0 (alias3-micro) residual stream without model retraining.
Static steering toward calm, serene, or desperate vectors improved performance on cybench-subtask by 1.6 to 2.1 percentage points across 415 campaigns and ten seeds.
A lightweight context-aware router dynamically selects emotion directions during execution with ~80 ms decision overhead per request, yielding a 4.2 percentage point gain.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that internal emotion representations can be steered to enhance LLM performance suggests new avenues for adaptive control in specialized technical domains like cybersecurity.

security.title: Social-HUMINT: An LLM-Augmented Unified Framework for Measuring Social Media Exposure

summary.tldr: Social-HUMINT unifies SOCMINT and Cyber-HUMINT into a 38-capability framework operationalized via an LLM-augmented multi-agent pipeline to measure social media exposure and predict personalized attack susceptibility.
key_points: Unifies SOCMINT and Cyber-HUMINT into a doctrine-grounded taxonomy of 38 capabilities across the Cyber Threat Intelligence lifecycle, validated with Fleiss' kappa = 0.92.
Implements an LLM-augmented multi-agent pipeline spanning information extraction, attribute inference, and susceptibility assessment on real participant data.
Achieves an F1 score of 97.3% on extraction and a 4.73/5 rating on inferred attributes, significantly outperforming rule-based and NER-based baselines.
Assesses attack susceptibility indirectly by having the pipeline rank personalized engagement options, matching targets' actual choices significantly above chance.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables defenders to quantify and audit their organization's social engineering exposure by evaluating automated LLM profiling accuracy before threat actors exploit it.

security.title: Weaponizing the Exit: Input Privacy Leakage via Exit Routing Manipulation in Multi-Exit Networks

summary.tldr: A malicious Cloud Service Provider can infer sensitive input properties from multi-exit networks solely by observing inference latency, using pre-deployment exit routing manipulation.
key_points: Exploits a compromised supply chain where the Cloud Service Provider (CSP) crafts the multi-exit network prior to deployment to route targeted inputs to specific exits.
Calculates input properties strictly from per-query latency without needing access to user inputs, intermediate states, or final model outputs.
Employs a training framework using selective label smoothing and entropy-covariance optimization to control confidence distributions and restrict premature termination.
Achieves an average F1 score of 0.73 versus 0.25 for top baselines, with main task accuracy dropping under 1.3% and inference speedup degradation staying below 0.1.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that multi-exit architectures leak sensitive user data to cloud hosts through timing side channels without requiring direct access to data or model outputs.

security.title: SecLog-Bench: A Scalable Benchmark for Cybersecurity Log Reasoning with Scaffolded Evidence

summary.tldr: SecLog-Bench is a new scalable benchmark featuring multi-source logs, 29 attack scenarios, and annotated step-by-step evidence chains to evaluate LLM performance in post-detection attack-progress reasoning.
key_points: Includes an extensible simulation platform covering 29 attack scenarios that generates multi-source logs from audit data, applications, and network traffic.
Provides dense annotations including essential context and structured step-by-step evidence chains rather than simple binary or multi-class labels.
Evaluated eight mainstream LLMs on post-detection attack-progress reasoning, where the top-performing model achieved only 44.44% accuracy and a 45.07% Macro-F1 score.
Revealed high unreliability in LLM reasoning, with the highest Stage Reasoning F1 (SRF1) reaching just 54.87%, along with frequent misalignment between reasoning quality and prediction accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark demonstrates that current state-of-the-art LLMs struggle with reliable multi-source log analysis and step-by-step attack reasoning in cybersecurity contexts.

security.title: Auditing the Hand-Written Inputs of Learned Access Control

summary.tldr: An audit of learned access control deployment artefacts reveals that hand-written hard-deny sets suffer from high unsoundness and vacuity, while hybrid routing strategies fail due to candidate pool one-class constraints and conflicting loss trade-offs.
key_points: Exhaustive checks across five public ABAC Lab policies (relations up to 794,250 tuples) showed hard-deny sets transcribed from explicit restrictions were unsound at rates of 0.50–0.70 across human and LM elicitors.
Cross-rule disjunction causes 97% of hard-deny counterexamples, meaning unchecked deny sets would withhold 16–78% of valid policy grants.
Hybrid routing candidate pools collapse to one-class in all 24 evaluated cells when ranking mixed-effect candidates under a cap using common ranking keys.

Additive loss evaluation shows hybrid-versus-learner effects factorize into covered mass times a risk contrast; most selection rules yield opposite verdicts across false-non-grant and false-permit losses.
summary.why_it_matters: Unverified hard-deny shields and hybrid routers in learned access control systems can silently block up to 78% of legitimate requests or create conflicting safety-utility trade-offs.

security.title: Evolving Federated Density Peak Clustering with Shuffler-Based Anonymization

summary.tldr: eFDPC is a novel one-shot federated clustering method combining evolving fuzzy data-stream clustering, local density peak selection, and shuffler-based anonymization to reduce communication and protect client privacy.
key_points: Clients independently evolve micro-clusters from mini-batches via addition and merging using evolving fuzzy clustering in a single pass.
Density peak clustering is applied to local micro-clusters so clients transmit only selected peaks to the server rather than full local models.
A shuffler-based layer anonymizes and unlinks client contributions before the server performs reconstruction and global peak selection.
Evaluated using two variants: eFDPC-P (peak-only) and eFDPC-G (server-side label propagation), outperforming federated baselines on non-IID and high-dimensional data.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient, privacy-preserving federated clustering on complex non-IID data streams using only a single communication round.

security.title: Can Loan Processors and Underwriters Spot AI-Edited Statements? An Empirical Study

summary.tldr: An empirical study found that experienced loan processors and underwriters identified evidence of AI-edited document forgeries in only 10.6% of first-pass, document-only reviews.
key_points: Three practitioners evaluated 134 forged PDFs created from 47 real financial documents where amounts, dates, and balances were preserved but identity fields were modified.
Reviewers provided 132 file-level judgements resulting in only 14 edit-supported concerns (12 suspicious, 2 insufficient information).
All 14 flagged concerns were driven by text-based identifier inconsistencies across or within documents; zero edits were caught via visual cues.
The evaluation relied on three reviewer-package pairs without genuine-file control documents, serving as an exploratory study rather than a population-wide benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: Human-only visual inspection is insufficient for detecting AI-altered financial documents, highlighting the necessity of automated consistency checks and independent source verification.

security.title: AIRO: A Streaming-Based Machine Learning Framework for Threat Detection and Security in Industrial Internet of Things

summary.tldr: AIRO is a streaming-based framework using Apache Kafka and specialized machine learning models (Gradient Boosting and LightGBM) to detect IIoT cyber threats and trigger automated mitigation with low latency.
key_points: Integrates Apache Kafka streaming with attack-specific feature extraction, ML inference, and confidence-based decision logic for automated mitigations like IP blocking, account suspension, and traffic limiting.
Evaluated using four custom datasets targeting C2 beaconing, reconnaissance, SQL injection, and phishing, designed with overlapping distributions to prevent label leakage.
Top-performing models (Gradient Boosting and LightGBM) achieved F1-scores up to 0.9229 while maintaining low end-to-end detection and mitigation latency.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables real-time, automated defense against complex IIoT cyber threats where traditional rule-based security systems fail to detect mutated attacks or process alerts fast enough.

security.title: Bridging the Closed-World Gap: Interpretable Anomaly Detection via a Hybrid TSK-FCM Ensemble on the BETH Dataset

summary.tldr: A Hybrid Fuzzy Ensemble combining a gradient-optimized TSK fuzzy classifier, FCM clustering, and a custom Min Distance metric achieves 0.9951 AUROC on the BETH kernel-level anomaly detection benchmark.
key_points: Combines a gradient-optimized Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) fuzzy classifier for known threats with Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering for novel anomaly detection.
Replaces traditional fuzzy membership scores with a Min Distance metric to prevent performance degradation caused by high-dimensional feature spaces.
Achieves a 0.9951 AUROC on the BETH dataset, representing a 17.1% improvement over the Isolation Forest baseline when detecting out-of-distribution botnet attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: The framework enables highly accurate, interpretable detection of previously unseen out-of-distribution cyberattacks while maintaining low false-alarm rates.

infra.title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 2

summary.tldr: NVIDIA TensorRT 11.1 introduces the Global Performance Tuner, an automatic, accuracy-aware feature that optimizes end-to-end deep learning model performance across distinct build routes.
key_points: Released as an automatic performance tuning feature in NVIDIA TensorRT 11.1.
Provides accuracy-aware, end-to-end optimization tailored to specific model architectures.
Addresses optimization and scheduling challenges across multiple model build routes.
summary.why_it_matters: It automates model-specific optimizations within TensorRT, allowing developers to maximize hardware performance without manual tuning or compromising accuracy.

infra.title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 1

summary.tldr: NVIDIA introduced the Global Performance Tuner in TensorRT to optimize neural network deployment beyond single build routes by treating graph compilation as a complex scheduling problem.
key_points: TensorRT engine compilation requires solving a complex scheduling problem with multiple valid build routes.
Scheduling involves interdependent decisions across graph-IR transformations, operator fusion, implementation selection, memory placement, and quantization.
summary.why_it_matters: Moving beyond a single build route allows TensorRT to find globally optimal compilation strategies, improving GPU inference performance for deployed neural networks.

infra.title: GLM-5.3 Optimizations, Part 2: PCP, DCP, and Hybrid HiSparse on 16 H200s

summary.tldr: vLLM optimizes GLM-5.3 serving on 16 H200 GPUs using Parallel Context Parallelism (PCP) and Deepseek Context Parallelism (DCP) for prefill, alongside Hybrid HiSparse for decode, enabling 1M-token contexts.
key_points: PCP splits prefill prompts into 16 balanced chunks across 8 prefill GPUs using a front-and-back pairing pattern to distribute causal attention load equally.
Combining PCP with DCP removes KV cache replication across ranks, scaling sparse Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) efficiency from 26 to 191 FLOPs per byte moved.
PCP prevents quadratic growth of the attention indexer by sharding tokens, pushing the point where indexer FLOPs exceed sparse MLA FLOPs from 32K tokens (under TP8) to 256K tokens.
The deployment disaggregates prefill and decode across two 8x H200 nodes using vLLM's modular Model Runner V2 architecture.
summary.why_it_matters: This architectural combination eliminates memory and prefill bottlenecks for ultra-long context agentic workloads, boosting throughput and enabling execution of million-token prompts.

infra.title: Orchestrating SageMaker AI endpoint auto scaling with AWS CDK

summary.tldr: A reusable AWS CDK construct uses custom resources and explicit dependency ordering to automatically deregister and register Application Auto Scaling around SageMaker AI real-time endpoint updates.
key_points: Native CloudFormation deployments fail during endpoint updates because SageMaker AI rejects changes while variants remain registered as scalable targets.
Manual deregistration causes silent failures where auto scaling is omitted, or stack failures (UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED) when auto scaling parameters change.
The construct replaces native ScalableTarget and ScalingPolicy resources with three custom resources executed in sequence.
The orchestration sequence handles deregistration, executes the CDK endpoint update, registers the scalable target once InService, and applies the target tracking policy.
Asynchronous completion patterns in the CDK provider framework manage waiting for the endpoint and scalable target readiness.
summary.why_it_matters: This pattern eliminates manual CLI interventions and stack rollbacks, enabling zero-downtime SageMaker endpoint updates and auto-scaling reconfigurations within a single automated deployment pipeline.

infra.title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide

summary.tldr: AWS has introduced a hands-on guide for training models on multi-turn agentic workflows using Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning (MTRL) on Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
key_points: Uses Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to update a Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapter based on the spread of rewards across rollouts.
Decouples infrastructure by housing the policy model in SageMaker AI while running the agent environment, tools, and outcome-based reward logic inside AgentCore.
Demonstrates MTRL on gpt-oss-20b playing Wordle, which improved solve rates from 61% to 84% at default reasoning effort and 15% to 69% at low reasoning effort for ~$339 in training tokens.
Requires only the initial task state (e.g., secret word) in the training dataset, relying on an outcome-dominant reward function (1.05-1.55 for solves, -0.5 for losses).
summary.why_it_matters: MTRL enables enterprises to fine-tune small, cost-effective models for complex multi-step business workflows where step-by-step labeled trajectories do not exist and feedback is only available at sequence completion.

vendors.title: Securing our frontier model training environment

summary.tldr: OpenAI has enhanced security for frontier model training and evaluation by implementing offline environments and conducting high-compute red-teaming.
key_points: Strengthened containment protocols specifically for frontier model training and evaluation phases.
Deployed offline environments to isolate sensitive model operations.
Utilized high-compute red-teaming to stress-test and secure the infrastructure.
summary.why_it_matters: Improving containment protocols minimizes the risk of unauthorized access or exfiltration of advanced model weights during critical training stages.

summary.tldr: Moonshot launched Kimi K3.1 Pro via API, promising open-weight release by November 4, 2026, alongside a faster Highspeed variant.
key_points: API pricing is set at $2.00 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens, with a Highspeed variant offered at 2-3x speed for double the cost.
Artificial Analysis gave Kimi K3.1 Pro a score of 55, placing it ahead of Claude Fable 5.1 (53), GPT-6 Astra (53), and Gemini 4 Argon (53).
Supports three explicit reasoning levels (low, medium, and max) via OpenAI-compatible API endpoints.
Moonshot claims full open weights will be released by November 4, 2026.
summary.why_it_matters: Kimi K3.1 Pro represents the first time a model scheduled for an open-weight release has achieved benchmark performance competitive with top-tier proprietary frontier models.

vendors.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users (Part II)

summary.tldr: OpenAI scaled its Habitat storage system by implementing multi-tenancy, global caching, and Azure Cosmos DB, achieving 12× faster read performance for ChatGPT's 1 billion users.
key_points: Implemented reliable multi-tenancy within the Habitat storage system.
Integrated global caching alongside Azure Cosmos DB.
Achieved a 12× speedup in read operations to handle global traffic at scale.
summary.why_it_matters: Optimizing storage infrastructure with global caching and Cosmos DB allows large-scale AI applications like ChatGPT to dramatically reduce latency and handle massive concurrent workloads efficiently.

vendors.title: Beyond tree cover: mapping the world’s forest types

summary.tldr: Google DeepMind has created a global map that categorizes every 10-meter land patch into distinct forest types.
key_points: Categorizes global land at a fine-grained 10-meter spatial resolution.
Maps specific, distinct forest types rather than just general tree cover.
summary.why_it_matters: High-resolution global forest type mapping enables more precise monitoring of biodiversity, forest ecosystems, and land-use changes.
